Background Streaming and Streaming CSV

Background Streaming

In Tool Setup, select Enable Background Streaming for a Meters or Scopes Tool Instance. Meters offers six acquisition modes. Scopes Background captures read-only numeric Measure cycles, not screenshots or waveforms. Powers and Wavegen do not support Background. A Background instance cannot also be used by foreground Tool actions. Existing steps are retained when switching roles; resolve the displayed conflict before running. Turning off Background while another mode is selected requires choosing Single before using foreground Measure. Two instances cannot share one Live resource in a run.

Choose Finite or Infinite. For Scopes, Finite Cycles counts complete measurement cycles, each containing all selected Channel/Item pairs; Infinite continues until Worker OFF or Stop Workflow. Set Measure interval (seconds) (default 1) as the wait after a complete cycle, not a precise sample rate. In Measurements, add or remove rows and select each Channel and Item from the Scopes capabilities. Each row has an internal stable Measurement ID. Individual measurements in a cycle are read sequentially. Scopes validates supported items and channel/model parameters when starting.

For Meters, Finite Simple modes use Max Samples; finite Custom modes use Trigger Count, with Sample Count readings per trigger. Infinite Custom requires explicit Allow Buffer Overflow Risk. Infinite Background acquisition has no hidden Simulation sample limit.

Software and Software Custom use Timer Interval (ms) by default, initially 1000. The first trigger is sent when the source is ready. After one reading or a complete Custom batch arrives, Orchestrator waits the selected interval before the next trigger. This is a delay between completed measurements, not a fixed sampling frequency. Capture OFF leaves triggering and optional Live Monitor running. Worker OFF, Stop Workflow, source completion or failure stops triggering. A rejected trigger or measurement timeout fails the run and preserves available data. For Software Simple, Trigger with BG Command replaces this timer with Workflow commands; enable FG/BG Interaction in Workflow before using it.

External and External Custom use the connected trigger signal in Live. Simulation generates virtual triggers on supported models, including 34461A; 34460A does not support External. Slope and delay settings are passed to the tool. Simulation does not verify physical trigger timing.

Live Monitor is optional and starts unchecked. For Scopes, the Monitor has a Measurement selector and plots one numeric field at a time, independently of Capture; an invalid reading is not plotted as zero. The Allow Risk warning in 5.1 Meters Setup applies to Custom Background sources. Lost readings cannot be recovered by Stop; check captured counts and data quality after stopping.

Add these Workflow actions and select the Background in Step Properties:

  • Worker ON starts its source at that Step. For Scopes, it launches the streaming Worker, applies existing Scopes Setup while the stream waits, then starts Measure Streaming after Setup succeeds. Simultaneous Capture ON starts unchecked; check it to retain the first samples from startup.
  • Capture ON starts a new Dataset while the Worker continues independently.
  • Capture OFF finishes that Dataset and its optional streaming CSV without stopping the Worker or automatically exporting another file.
  • Worker OFF releases the source. Simultaneous Capture OFF starts checked. Uncheck it if Capture was already explicitly switched OFF. Stopping a finite source before its configured count is reached fails the run; use Stop Workflow to end the run early and retain a partial Dataset.

Repeated ON/OFF is a Step error. A finite source automatically retains its tail and finishes its Dataset. The first subsequent Capture OFF acknowledges that automatic finish; the first Worker OFF releases the source. A second explicit OFF fails. An ended source cannot Capture ON again until Worker OFF and a new Worker ON. Every run also cleans up remaining Workers, including on failure, while preserving the existing Powers Safe-Off behavior.

The optional FG/BG Data Buffer is independent of Capture and Live Monitor. See Background Interaction Steps for its fixed capacity, FIFO/Ring modes, overflow and read rules.

Output contains Charts, optional Live Monitors, Foreground Output, and Background Output as separate expandable sections. Background-only runs can use Charts and Background Output. Background Output appears only when the Last Run had Background bindings; changing the current Draft does not hide those results. Its Background and Capture Dataset selectors control its Summary, Output Data and export, independently of each Chart's selection.

Foreground Output has a Source card with an Output Page selector, the current page number, and short guidance. Changing the Output Page updates its Summary, Output Data, and selected-page export. Background Output has a Source card for its Background and Capture Dataset selectors and Worker status. Both outputs place their export options under Export settings below Output Data.

Background numeric Summary and Output Data use the same styled tables as Foreground. Background numeric values share the Auto, Fixed, and Raw Number display setting, without changing stored data or export precision. Background Summary shows only statistics already present in the Dataset, including Scopes valid and invalid counts; Serial RX shows event and byte counts instead. Background still reads 100 rows per page, independently of Foreground Output Pages.

Background Source places Background and Capture Dataset side by side when space permits and wraps them on narrow windows. Pagination controls appear only for Datasets exceeding 100 rows and use the standard action-button style. Foreground Export settings explains whether the selected option opens a file or folder picker; Background Export settings always selects a destination folder and exports the complete selected or all Datasets, not just the visible rows. The Background export button shows the chosen format.

In Charts, use Chart settings to choose Ground (Foreground or Background), then Page (a Foreground Output Page or Background source), and select Add Chart. Each Chart displays a colored Foreground or Background source label and its Page or Background ID. The Save charts with template option and shared chart count appear at the top-right of Charts. All Foreground Pages and Background Charts appear together in Chart number order, regardless of source. Each Background Chart offers Export PNG, Settings, Source settings, and Remove. Source settings shows the selected Background as read-only and offers Capture Dataset and X-axis data (Elapsed Time, Timestamp or Sample Index). Scopes adds a Measurement selector. The Background source is chosen when the Chart is created; when unavailable in the current Draft or Last Run, use Reassign source to select a valid Background present in both. Changes apply immediately, and the Chart card retains its source badge and Data summary. Each Scopes Chart selects one Measurement field; use multiple Charts to plot different measurements rather than combining different units on one axis. Background Charts can be removed down to zero. Choose Line, XY Scatter, Column, Area or Bar in Settings; only Line updates during a run. Foreground retains all its existing chart types. Each Chart initially selects the latest available Dataset for its Background and then keeps that selection, even if newer Datasets arrive. Each new run chooses afresh. With no Dataset, the Chart waits for captured data and never substitutes Monitor samples.

Background X uses actual Elapsed Time in seconds, Timestamp, or Sample Index. Hover identifies an actual displayed sample. Line/Area retain peaks, troughs and endpoints when sampled; Scatter/Column/Bar show representative observations. Data summary shows Total samples, In range and Plotted, with the current sampling status. Line/Area/Column Zoom requests detail for the visible range; Scatter/Bar have no Zoom controls. Line Settings → General → Show All Raw Data displays all visible samples up to 25,000. Above this limit the Chart shows no points and asks you to narrow Zoom or turn the option off. Full Dataset storage and CSV/XLSX export are unchanged.

Last Run Charts remain viewable and editable after removing their binding from the current Workflow. Display settings never recreate or modify Draft bindings. With Save charts with template enabled, a Chart referring to a Background missing from the Draft prevents Template Save and identifies the Chart to fix. Remove that Chart, select a valid source, or turn off saving Charts.

When enabled in Setup, Live Monitors appears immediately below Charts as a separate expandable framed section with matching inner cards. Charts and Live Monitors collapse independently; without any enabled Monitor, the section is hidden. Each monitor has a compact Monitor info section: numeric monitors describe the latest-1,000-Worker-sample buffer, while Serial RX monitors describe their bounded-byte buffer. Both operate independently of Capture. Numeric monitors retain Line appearance, Hover and Zoom, and continue updating while Capture is OFF. Worker OFF stops updates; restarting a Worker clears its Monitor. It has no Chart Settings, Add/Remove, saved Chart, PNG, Dataset, Summary, CSV or XLSX, and consumes no Chart slot. Summary in Background Output shows Dataset count/min/max/average, status and quality for Meters. For Scopes, it shows valid/invalid counts and min/max/average per Measurement field. The Scopes Output Data table displays the selected fields and leaves invalid values blank, with the reason available on hover. Output Data uses pages of 100 rows. no_loss_detected describes the Tool's evidence, not a zero-loss guarantee.

Capture boundaries follow received event processing, not hardware sample time. Full captured samples stay in memory for the current run. A new run or Clear Last Run releases them; there is no history or recovery store. Background samples do not feed Workflow variables, calculations, assertions or ResultRows.

CSV Export → Stream Background CSV during Capture is independent of foreground CSV. Choose All Backgrounds or one Background and its output folder. The default is <application folder>/data. For Scopes, Scopes CSV columns selects Values + units or Values + units + validity + reason before Run; the latter includes per-Measurement quality fields. Both formats retain blank values for invalid measurements rather than writing zero. Meters retains its existing five-column CSV. Each Capture creates a new CSV; Monitor-only operation creates none. Every enabled CSV destination follows the failure policy below and keeps any partial files.

After the run, Export Background saves the selected or all Datasets as CSV or XLSX, including partial data from a failed run. When a Scopes Dataset is present, Scopes export columns lets each manual export choose the same two formats independently of the format used during streaming; captured memory data always retains value, unit, valid and reason. More than 300,000 samples shows a warning. XLSX defaults to 300,000 samples per file; edit Samples per XLSX file from 1 to 1,048,575. Larger Datasets split into new files without truncation. Export names avoid overwriting streaming or previous manual files. No Capture OFF or run completion automatically performs manual export.

9. Streaming CSV

Streaming CSV is configured in the Workflow area's CSV Export panel. It is different from exporting a completed run later. The panel starts collapsed when the application opens. Click its title to expand or collapse it; collapsing only hides the controls and does not change their values.

Foreground streaming requires at least one Output; Background streaming does not. Choose one of these foreground modes:

  • Selected Page — choose one Output Page and optionally choose an output folder. Desktop automatically creates a timestamped CSV filename. The selected Page is fixed once the run starts.
  • All Pages — optionally choose an output folder. Desktop creates a timestamped destination directory and one CSV file for each Page.

If no folder is selected, Streaming output uses the application's data folder:

Default output folder: <application folder>/data

Streaming behavior:

  • Headers are created and flushed before workflow execution.
  • Only committed ResultRows are written.
  • Each written row is flushed.
  • Any enabled CSV creation, write or final-flush failure fails the run, stops further ordinary Steps and performs background and Powers safety cleanup. It is independent of Graceful Loop Stop and preserves committed rows, received Background samples and partial CSV files.
  • CSV data already written from committed rows remains after workflow failure or Stop Workflow / loop Stop.
  • Streaming does not produce XLSX files.
  • Streaming settings are locked while the run is active.
